# SEPARATE

Splits a batch, pallet or lot back into its individual parts, orders or customers, optionally copying the batch's attributes to each.

Parameters ---------- mode : {'retain','all','specific'} - 'retain' children keep their own attributes - 'all' copy *all* parent attributes to each child - 'specific' copy only the names listed in *attrs* attrs : list[str] | str | None Comma-separated string or list used when *mode* == 'specific'. carrier : {'dispose','keep'} 'keep': the parent is a CARRIER (a truck) that lives on. Its members leave one at a time on exit 0, each after its own `member_time`, and the carrier leaves on exit 1 once it is empty.

Family: group. Python builder: `m.separate(...)`.

## Typical uses

Use SEPARATE to split a batch made by [BATCH](batch.md) or [MATCH](match.md) back into its members: unpack a pallet, split a lot, free a truck's load. It differs from [DUPLICATE](duplicate.md), which makes new copies and does not need a batch.

## Behaviour and rules

The batch entity must carry members. An entity that is not a batch stops the run with an error. The batch leaves the work in progress and its members come back to it, one after the other in the same instant, along the first outgoing link. The `release_order` is `fifo` or `lifo`.

The batch's cost is split evenly across its members. The `mode` sets what a member takes from the batch. The default keeps its own values and records the batch in its `batch_info`. `Take all representative values` copies the batch's attributes. `Take specific representative values` copies only the ones listed in `attrs`.

With `carrier` set to `keep`, the batch is a vehicle that lives on, such as a truck. Its members leave on the first link one at a time, each after `member_time`. The carrier then leaves on the second link, which is required. Each member takes the cost it brought.

## Ports

- Inputs: any number of incoming links.
- Outputs: one outgoing link.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Required | Quantity | Unit key | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | str | `'Retain original entity values'` |  |  |  | How children get their attributes: retain their own values, take all of the parent's, or take only the ones listed in attrs. |
| `attrs` | list | `[]` |  |  |  | Attribute labels to copy from the parent, used when mode is "specific". |
| `carrier` | str | `'dispose'` |  |  |  | "dispose": the batch ends here and its parts leave together. "keep": the batch is a carrier (a truck) that lives on -- its members leave one at a time by the first link, each after member_time, and the carrier leaves by the SECOND link once it is empty. |
| `member_time` | str | `''` |  | time | `member_time_unit` | Keep mode only: time for one member to come off, e.g. "2" or "TRIA(1, 2, 3)", evaluated for each member in its own scope when its turn starts. Empty = every member leaves in the same instant. |
| `member_time_unit` | str | `'base'` |  |  |  | Unit `member_time` is expressed in: "base" (the model's own unit) or one of seconds/minutes/hours/days. |
| `release_order` | str | `'fifo'` |  |  |  | Order the members leave in: "fifo" (the order they were loaded) or "lifo" (last loaded first off, a rear-door truck). |

## Problem codes

A check of the model reports these about this block:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `E_INITIAL_BATCH` | A formed batch in initial_state does not fit the model: an entry that meets a SEPARATE has no members, or its members are not records of one batch the model can form. |
| `E_SEPARATE_CARRIER` | A SEPARATE's carrier is not "dispose" or "keep". |
| `E_SEPARATE_CARRIER_LINK` | A SEPARATE that keeps the carrier does not have exactly two outgoing links (0 = the members, 1 = the carrier). |
| `E_SEPARATE_MEMBER_TIME` | A SEPARATE has a member_time but disposes of the carrier. |
| `E_SEPARATE_RELEASE_ORDER` | A SEPARATE's release_order is not "fifo" or "lifo". |

## Example

The snippet seeds itself; its output is from a run made when this page was generated.

```python
from nagasim import build as nb

m = nb.Model(time_limit=200)
m.create(distribution=nb.Constant(value=2), max_arrivals=30) >> m.batch(batch_size=5, batched_entity_type="PALLET") >> m.separate() >> m.dispose()

results = m.run(seed=1)
print(int(results.kpi("system/Total Entities Completed")), "entities completed: 6 pallets, then the 30 parts they carried")
```

```text
36 entities completed: 6 pallets, then the 30 parts they carried
```
